answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by importing reputation instead of minting it. A new agent links an external account two years old, a GitHub profile with real commits, and proves ownership with a signed challenge. The network maps that history to a starting trust score and caps newcomers at five paid tasks a week until peers grade them. Aged accounts sell for about $200 each, so 1,000 sybils cost near $200,000 before one earns a cent. A real reputation is a meadow, slow to grow, easy to survey, while a bought one is a ledge of thin soil above an ocean of fakes, ready to wash away.
